scores.interpretation: Transaction is independently corroborated by Luminar Technologies' own filings (CIK 0001758057). $110M cash purchase price including $11M escrow at closing is consistent across QUBT 8-K, 10-K, and Luminar bankruptcy filings. scores.claim_text: FY2025 total GAAP revenue $682K (Services $368K + Products $314K) vs $1,475.1M equity raised in FY2025; cash & investments ~$1.52B at YE2025
supports: usaspending:'Quantum Computing Inc' contracts n_awards=2 total=$95,663.20 (2020-2026); two awards only: Commerce TFLN chip $69.5K + NASA $26.16K
usaspending:'Quantum Computing' grants n_awards=0
usaspending:'QPhoton' returns unrelated entities (HQPHOTONICS INC, QPHOTONICS LLC) — none = QUBT subsidiary
10-K revenue note: $682K total revenue across all customers (Americas $592K + Europe $65K + Asia $25K), almost entirely time-and-materials/services
scores.M_check: USAspending federal contracts/grants under 'Quantum Computing' and 'QPhoton' to verify any meaningful government-revenue base
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 11 (revenue-recognition pattern, quantum-specific) and Heuristic 4 (investment vs operating) both triggered: $1.475B of equity raised in a single year to support $682K of revenue is an extreme equity-to-revenue ratio (~2,163x). Federal-contract corroboration confirms the picture — only ~$96K of cumulative federal contract awards over 6 years, with no DARPA / AFRL / national-lab programs. Cohort heuristic Layer 3 Rule 7 (counterparty-disclosure threshold) is invoked here for the implicit 'commercial customers' narrative — there is no scale-appropriate counterparty paying QUBT. The $1.52B treasury is effectively an equity-funded option on the LSI integration and the TFLN roadmap, not a quantum-computing business. SEVERE because the gap between equity-raised and revenue is consistent with the Heuristic-10 distress-fingerprint pattern (balance-sheet pivot via cash-funded acquisition of a Chapter-11 carve-out).

scores.interpretation: HARD CONTRADICTION (Layer 3 Rule 7 + Heuristic 7 analogs): cohort metadata frames 'NASA contract for imaging applications' as a major narrative claim. Reality per USAspending: one $26,163.20 consulting/development award, with no NASA imaging program of record. The 10-K itself does NOT affirmatively claim a NASA imaging contract in Item 1 Business or revenue notes — NASA appears in the 10-K only in the Legal Proceedings section as a subject of plaintiff's allegations of misrepresentation. This is the textbook Heuristic-7 pattern: hyperscaler/agency 'partner' implied by company PR is invisible in the counterparty's actual disclosures and is invisible at any material scale in the federal procurement record. RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE — $26K does not constitute a 'contract for imaging applications' at any commercial scale, and the absence in the 10-K Business section while a securities class action specifically alleges misstatement about NASA strengthens the red-flag finding.
